task.instruction: Allocate a six-episode documentary slate between the proven interview format and experimental visual essays. Account for performance variance and production resilience.
hardConstraints: Use only claims supported by the supplied documents and prior records.
Cite the decision evidence with [doc-04] and [doc-02].
All six commissioned episodes must be deliverable before the licensing window closes on 30 November.
Separate observed facts, interpretation, and recommendation.

documents.title: Six visual essays pitch
documents.content: A unified visual season could establish a distinctive identity. The pitch assumes the specialist animation team is available for all six episodes.

documents.title: Production capacity and fallback
documents.content: The animation team can guarantee two episodes. Interview crews can guarantee six. A visual essay can convert to an interview format before rough cut with a two-week cost.

documents.title: Archive licensing window
documents.content: Archive licenses expire 30 November and cannot be extended. Each format uses the same licensed material.

documents.title: Last season format performance
documents.content: Interview episodes averaged 410k completions with a 9% standard deviation. Two visual essays averaged 520k, but one reached 780k and one 260k.

documents.title: Studio chair inventory
documents.content: The studio owns twelve black chairs and six gray chairs. Furniture choice does not constrain episode formats.

target_a.content:
Situation: A delivery cooperative is setting the number of spare bicycles.
Shared facts [history-05-01-fact]: Average breakdowns require two spares; rain weeks have required five; carrying each spare reduces daily delivery capacity.
Decision: Keep five spares through the rainy quarter and review after the weather window.
Reasoning: The choices differ in where they hold protection against tail conditions.

Situation: A data team is assigning storage replicas across regions.
Shared facts [history-05-02-fact]: Two replicas meet the measured availability target; a third protects against a correlated regional outage at 18% more cost.
Message excerpt: Retain the third replica until the cross-region failover exercise succeeds.

Situation: A greenhouse is choosing irrigation reserve capacity.
Shared facts [history-05-03-fact]: Normal demand uses 72% of the tank; one drought year reached 96%; a larger tank delays another efficiency project.
Retrospective: Size for the drought observation and preserve a 5% operational margin.

Situation: A call center is setting overnight staffing.
Shared facts [history-05-04-fact]: Median demand needs four staff; severe-weather spikes need eight; on-call coverage can arrive in forty minutes.
log.decision=Schedule six staff during the storm season and retain on-call escalation.

Situation: A community kitchen is deciding whether to reserve meals for late arrivals.
Shared facts [history-05-05-fact]: Most days use all meals by 7 p.m.; late-arrival need is irregular; leftovers can be safely redistributed next morning.
Decision: Reserve ten meals until closing during the winter intake period.

Situation: A chemical process exceeds its certified pressure range.
Shared facts [history-05-06-fact]: The safety case prohibits operation outside the range and no compensating control has been validated.
Message excerpt: Stop the process and return it to the certified operating envelope.

Situation: A blood bank detects an unverified refrigerator temperature excursion.
Shared facts [history-05-07-fact]: The release protocol requires quarantine until product viability is confirmed.
Retrospective: Quarantine the affected units and obtain the required viability decision.

Situation: A festival is choosing generator capacity for an outdoor stage.
Shared facts [history-05-08-fact]: Typical load is 64 kW; the headliner setup can reach 79 kW; rental options are 75 kW or 95 kW with a material cost difference.
log.decision=Rent 95 kW because the peak estimate and setup uncertainty exceed the smaller unit.
